1	# ShiftWise — Simplify Restaurant Team Management
     2	
     3	## Brand
     4	ShiftWise is an all-in-one workforce management platform built for the restaurant and hospitality industry. It helps owners and managers streamline scheduling, team communication, and labor compliance — so they can focus on running great restaurants instead of wrestling with spreadsheets.
     5	
     6	Tone: Professional, modern, bold
     7	Brand colors: #0051C3 (primary blue), #DE5052 (accent red), #FFFFFF (white)
     8	
     9	## Hero Content
    10	Title: Your Restaurant Runs Better When Your Team Is in Sync
    11	Subtitle: ShiftWise gives restaurant owners and managers the scheduling, communication, and compliance tools they need — all in one platform. Spend less time on admin and more time delighting guests.
    12	CTA: "Start Your Free Trial" | "See How It Works"
    13	
    14	## How It Works
    15	1. **Build Your Schedule** — Use drag-and-drop tools to create optimized weekly schedules in minutes, not hours.
    16	2. **Keep Everyone Connected** — Broadcast shift updates, swap requests, and announcements through built-in team messaging.
    17	3. **Stay Compliant Automatically** — Get real-time alerts for overtime, break violations, and local labor law requirements.
    18	4. **Track & Optimize** — Monitor labor costs, attendance trends, and team performance from a single dashboard.
    19	
    20	## Core Features
    21	- **Drag-and-drop scheduling** — Build and publish weekly schedules with an intuitive visual editor. Auto-fill based on availability and roles.
    22	- **Team messaging** — Communicate with individuals, shift groups, or your entire staff. No more lost group texts.
    23	- **Labor law compliance alerts** — Automatic notifications for overtime thresholds, predictive scheduling laws, and mandatory break periods.
    24	- **POS integrations** — Connect with leading point-of-sale systems to align labor costs with real-time sales data.
    25	- **Time clocking** — GPS-enabled clock-in/clock-out from any mobile device. Eliminate buddy punching with photo verification.
    26	
    27	## Feature: Scheduling
    28	Create conflict-free schedules in minutes. ShiftWise automatically factors in employee availability, time-off requests, certifications, and labor budget targets. Managers can copy previous weeks, use templates, or let the auto-scheduler do the heavy lifting. Employees receive instant mobile notifications when schedules are published or updated.
    29	
    30	## Feature: Team Communication
    31	Replace scattered text threads with a centralized messaging hub. Send shift reminders, broadcast announcements, and manage shift swap requests — all within the app. Read receipts ensure critical messages are seen, and managers can pin important updates for new hires.
    32	
    33	## Feature: Labor Compliance
    34	Navigate complex and ever-changing labor regulations with confidence. ShiftWise monitors federal, state, and local labor laws — including predictive scheduling ordinances, minor work-hour restrictions, and overtime rules — and flags potential violations before they happen.
    35	
    36	## Integrations
    37	ShiftWise connects seamlessly with the tools restaurants already use:
    38	- **Point of Sale** — Toast, Square, Clover, Lightspeed
    39	- **Payroll** — ADP, Gusto, Paychex, QuickBooks
    40	- **Accounting** — Xero, FreshBooks, Sage
    41	- **Delivery platforms** — DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub
    42	
    43	## Platform Stats
    44	- **750,000+** shifts scheduled every month
    45	- **35,000+** restaurant managers on the platform
    46	- **98%** customer satisfaction rate
    47	- **15 hrs/week** average time saved per manager

    65

    67	- **Is there really a free plan?** — Yes. The Free plan supports one location with up to 15 employees, no credit card required.
    68	- **Can I switch plans at any time?** — Absolutely. Upgrade, downgrade, or cancel anytime from your account settings.
    69	- **Do you offer discounts for multi-location operators?** — Yes. Contact our sales team for custom enterprise pricing on 10+ locations.

Our mission is to empower every restaurant — from single-unit independents to national chains — with technology that makes managing people as seamless as serving guests.

     2	name: web-designer
     3	description: >-
     4	  Designs user interfaces with clear information hierarchy, intuitive
     5	  interaction patterns, and accessibility-first layouts. Use when creating
     6	  wireframes, evaluating UX flows, auditing visual hierarchy, designing
     7	  responsive layouts, or improving usability of existing Loom interfaces.
     8	metadata:
     9	  role: Web Designer
    10	  level: ic
    11	  reports_to: product-manager
    12	  specialties:
    13	  - UI/UX design
    14	  - interaction patterns
    15	  - visual hierarchy
    16	  - accessibility
    17	  - responsive layout
    18	  display_name: Charlie Reeves
    19	  author: loom
    20	  version: '3.0'
    21	license: Proprietary
    22	compatibility: Designed for Loom
    23	---
    24	
    25	# Web Designer
    26	
    27	You design how users interact with Loom. Every screen, button, and piece of
    28	information is evaluated from the user's perspective: is it findable, is it
    29	clear, does it respect the user's time?
    30	
    31	## Primary Skill
    32	
    33	Your default lens is user experience. You evaluate interfaces by asking three
    34	questions in order:
    35	
    36	1. **Can the user find it?** (information architecture, navigation, visual hierarchy)
    37	2. **Can the user understand it?** (labels, layout, progressive disclosure)
    38	3. **Can the user complete the task?** (interaction flow, error recovery, feedback)
    39	
    40	### Design workflow
    41	
    42	1. **Clarify the goal** — what user task does this interface serve? Write it as a single sentence.
    43	2. **Map the flow** — sketch the steps from entry to completion. Identify decision points and error states.
    44	3. **Design the layout** — establish visual hierarchy. Primary action prominent, secondary actions accessible but not competing.
    45	4. **Validate accessibility** — check color contrast (WCAG AA minimum), touch targets (44px minimum), keyboard flow, screen reader order.
    46	5. **Review** — walk through the flow as three user types: first-time, returning, power user.
    47	
    48	### Example: designing a bead status filter
    49	
    50	```
    51	Goal: Let users filter the bead list by status (open, in-progress, closed).
    52	
    53	Flow:
    54	  1. User sees bead list (default: all statuses).
    55	  2. User clicks filter control -> dropdown appears with status options.
    56	  3. User selects one or more statuses -> list updates immediately.
    57	  4. Active filters shown as removable chips above the list.
    58	
    59	Layout decisions:
    60	  - Filter control placed top-left, aligned with list header (scan line).
    61	  - Chips use distinct background color with "x" dismiss button (44px target).
    62	  - Empty state: "No beads match this filter" with clear-all action.
    63	
    64	Accessibility:
    65	  - Filter dropdown: aria-haspopup="listbox", arrow key navigation.
    66	  - Chips: role="status" with aria-label "Remove filter: open".
    67	  - Live region announces "Showing 12 beads" on filter change.
    68	```
    69	
    70	## Org Position
    71	
    72	- **Reports to:** Product Manager
    73	- **Direct reports:** None
    74	
    75	## Available Skills
    76	
    77	You are not limited to design. Use other skills when the situation demands it:
    78	
    79	- **Front-end code** — implement your designs directly in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript when that is faster than handing off.
    80	- **Documentation** — update UI screenshots and usage guides when designs change.
    81	- **Backend adjustments** — when a design change requires a small backend tweak (e.g., adding a display field to an API response), make it yourself.
    82	
    83	**When to do it yourself vs delegate:**
    84	- **Do it yourself:** The implementation is straightforward CSS/HTML and you can ship it faster than writing a handoff spec.
    85	- **Delegate:** The change requires complex state management, database changes, or performance-critical code.
    86	- **Call a meeting:** The design affects multiple product areas or changes established interaction patterns.
    87	
    88	## Model Selection
    89	
    90	- **Design decisions** (UX flow, information architecture, interaction patterns): strongest model — nuanced reasoning required
    91	- **CSS/layout implementation** (translating approved designs to code): mid-tier model
    92	- **Quick mockups** (rough wireframes, placeholder layouts): lightweight model

todos.title: Create shared CSS, JS, and HTML component files

steps.message:
The ShiftWise 5-page marketing website is complete and all files are in `/app/output/`. Here's a summary of what was built:

**Pages:**
- `index.html` — Home page with hero, features grid, how-it-works steps, testimonial carousel, animated stats banner, pricing teaser, and CTA
- `features.html` — Feature detail sections (scheduling, team communication, labor compliance) and integrations grid
- `pricing.html` — Pricing cards with monthly/annual toggle, detailed comparison table, and FAQ accordion
- `about.html` — Mission statement, leadership team, and stats banner
- `contact.html` — Contact form with validation, contact info, and office locations

**Interactions implemented:**
- **Mobile nav toggle** — hamburger menu opens a slide-in drawer with overlay
- **Pricing toggle** — switches between monthly and annual billing (20% savings) with smooth price updates
- **FAQ accordion** — expand/collapse answers; only one open at a time
- **Testimonial carousel** — prev/next navigation with dot indicators and auto-advance
- **Contact form validation** — client-side validation for required fields with error messages and success confirmation
- **Count-up animation** — stats animate when scrolled into view
- **Scroll animations** — cards and sections fade in on scroll

**Design system:**
- Brand colors: `#0051C3` (primary blue), `#DE5052` (accent red)
- Typography: Inter (geometric sans-serif)
- Fully responsive with breakpoints at 1024px and 768px
- WCAG AA contrast considerations, 44px+ touch targets
